vaultRoot.description:
Absolute vault root, used by the desktop runtime to resolve local assets
directly from disk (the web runtime uses the `/api/assets` route instead).

assetRoot.description: Vault-relative directory where downloaded assets are stored.

tagsField.description:
The resolved frontmatter key for the built-in tags field (configured via
`tags.field`, defaulting to `tags`). Clients use this for the tag editor,
the Library tag filter, and to hide tags from the generic "Details" view —
so the name lives in one place instead of being hardcoded per client.

HomeConfig.description:
The home page: just its sections. The page *title* is deliberately not
config — every client renders a localized "Home" (app copy, not user data).

criteria.description:
Smart-list-grade criteria (see [`crate::contract::SmartFilterGroup`]) —
the same rule model and evaluator as `.base` smart lists, stored
structurally here because the vault config is strict-parsed YAML, not a
Bases file. Absent means every entry of the type matches.

SmartFilterGroup.description:
A smart list's criteria: a conjunction over rules and (one level of)
subgroups. The type scope is *not* in here — it rides separately as
`scope` on the detail/requests and the server maintains its
`file.inFolder(...)` atom.

SmartFilterConjunction.description:
How a smart-list filter group combines its members: every rule must match,
any rule may match, or no rule may match (Bases `and`/`or`/`not`).

SmartFilterRule.description:
One smart-list criterion. Which of the optional members apply depends on
`kind`:

- `compare` — `field`, `op`, and exactly one of `value`/`number`/`boolean`/
  `date` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`)/`relative`.
- `contains` — `field`, `values` (with `mode`, default any-of).
- `startsWith` / `endsWith` — `field`, `values[0]`.
- `isEmpty` — `field` (`negated: true` reads as "has a value").
- `hasTag` — `values` (any listed tag).
- `linksTo` — `values[0]`: an entity basename/path the note must link to.
- `inFolder` — `values[0]`: a vault-relative folder.
- `unsupported` — `raw` only; preserved verbatim, ignored by evaluation.

`field` is a frontmatter key, or the special `file.name` / `file.mtime`.

negated.description:
Logical negation of the rule (supported on every kind but `compare`,
where the operator itself expresses it).

raw.description: `kind = unsupported`: the construct's raw YAML, round-tripped verbatim.

SmartFilterRuleKind.description:
The editable smart-list rule shapes. `unsupported` is the read-mostly
escape hatch: a construct the editor can't model, carried as raw YAML.

SmartRelativeDate.description:
A date relative to today: `amount`×`unit` into the past (default) or the
future (`future: true`) — "started in the last 90 days", "airing in the
next 2 weeks". On `file.mtime` rules it is relative to `now()` instead.

SmartDurationUnit.description: The calendar unit of a relative-date rule ("in the last N …").

SmartFilterSubgroup.description: A nested rule group — one level deep only (see the module note above).

log.description:
Daily-note logging config. **Its presence opts the type into logging** — the
quick-log / "check episode" flows write a line to the daily note only for
types that declare a `log` block. The type's hashtag lives as a literal in
`lineFormat`; unset fields fall back to `dailyNotes.log`. Resolve via
[`KizunaConfig::resolve_log_config`].

titleRole.description:
When `original`, the filename basename is the language-agnostic fallback
title (mirrors a title field's `titleRole`). The viewer's language picks
the displayed title; this is the floor when no language matches.

BodySection.description:
A declared section of an entity's Markdown body, addressed by its heading.
Generalizes the old `bodyMappings`: a flat struct discriminated by `kind`
(mirroring `FieldConfig`), so the same per-type mechanism covers
external-metadata sections *and* the built-in episodes/tracks list.

heading.description: The Markdown heading (text only, no `#`s) this section lives under.

externalFields.description:
`kind = external`: the provider field(s) that fill this heading. The matched
candidate's source is chosen, exactly like [`FieldConfig::external_fields`],
so one heading can be filled from multiple providers.

tracking.description: `kind = episodes`: how watched/read state is tracked. Defaults to `checklist`.

TypeLogConfig.description:
Per-type daily-note logging config, under `types[].log`. **Presence opts the
type into logging.** The type's hashtag is written as a literal inside
`lineFormat` (e.g. `- {title} {note} #Anime`), not a separate field —
so it's explicit, never inferred from the type name. Unset fields fall back to
`dailyNotes.log`, then the built-ins.

enumRole.description:
Semantic role of an `enum` field. `status` marks the one field the engine
treats as the entity's lifecycle status; behavior keys off this role, never
the field name. See [`EnumRole`] and `docs/status-role-plan.md`.

statusValues.description:
For an `enumRole: status` field: maps each canonical status to the user
option strings that mean it. Absent (or a canonical absent from it) leaves
that canonical unmapped — the field is still the status field, but no
canonical behavior fires. See [`StatusValues`].

EnumRole.description:
A field's semantic *role* beyond its raw `FieldType`. Currently only `status`:
it marks the one enum field the engine treats as the entity's lifecycle status.
Like `DateRole`/`TitleRole`, meaning flows from this role, never from the field
name. Kept a flat string enum so swift-openapi-generator renders proper cases.

StatusValues.description:
Maps each canonical status to the user-defined option strings that mean it. The
**first** option listed for a canonical is the *write target* — what a log flip
writes when it sets that status. An empty vec means that canonical is unmapped
(no behavior fires for it). Fixed optional keys (not an open map) for
codegen-friendliness and clean "unmapped" semantics.

app.description: The inline app config (vault root + write mode), owned by the runtime.

vaultConfigPath.description:
Path to the vault config file (`<vaultRoot>/KizunaShelf/config.yaml`).
`None` until a vault root is configured.

vaultExists.description: Whether the vault config file exists on disk.

AppConfig.description:
App-level configuration. Describes how *this machine* runs KizunaShelf and
where the vault lives on disk. This is owned by the runtime and passed
inline: env vars for web, the native vault switcher for desktop, and the
host app's local state for iOS. It is never stored in the synced vault config.

VaultConfig.description:
Vault-level configuration. Describes the vault's content schema (taxonomy,
assets, entity types, home dashboard, daily notes). Stored inside the vault
at `<vaultRoot>/KizunaShelf/config.yaml` so it travels with the vault and is
synced by the vault's own syncing method.

dateFormat.description:
Moment.js-style date format (as used by Obsidian Daily Notes) for the file
path relative to the daily-notes folder, without the `.md` extension —
e.g. `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to `YYYY-MM-DD`.

template.description:
Vault-relative path to a template used to seed a daily note that does not
exist yet (date tokens substituted). Absent → a new note starts empty.

log.description:
Global defaults for daily-note logging — the heading written under and the
line format. Per-type `log` blocks override these; see
[`KizunaConfig::resolve_log_config`].

DailyNoteLogDefaults.description:
Global defaults for daily-note logging, under `dailyNotes.log`. Both fields are
optional; a per-type [`TypeLogConfig`] overrides them, and the built-ins
([`DEFAULT_LOG_SECTION`] / [`DEFAULT_LOG_LINE_FORMAT`]) fill any remaining gap.

section.description:
Heading to write log lines under, as raw heading text (no `#`, default h2) —
consistent with `bodySections[].heading`.

lineFormat.description:
Line template. Tokens: `{title}` (the entity — **always rendered as a
`[[wikilink]]`**, since that link is what ties the line back to the entity;
write `{title}`, not `[[{title}]]`, though the latter isn't doubled),
`{note}` (freeform), `{date}`. Empty tokens collapse with surrounding
whitespace. There is no episode token — logging is independent of the
episode list, so put an episode number in `{note}` if you want one.

TagsConfig.description:
Configuration for the built-in **tags** field — a universal, cross-type label
list. Tags are a vault-level "well-known field": the *name* is configured here
(defaulting to `tags`), so the engine reads the field name from config rather
than hardcoding it. A schema field that happens to share this name is ignored
in favor of the built-in. This is a deliberate, narrow extension of the
schema-driven model — meaning still flows config → behavior, just at the vault
scope rather than the per-type scope.

field.description: The frontmatter key holding the entity's tag list. Defaults to `tags`.

vault.description:
The vault config (the schema) to write. The vault root and write mode are
owned by the runtime (env vars / the native vault switcher / `@AppStorage`),
so they are never sent here. Omitting `vault` is a no-op.

vaultExists.description: Whether the vault config file exists on disk.

content.description:
The raw YAML text of the config file, verbatim (empty when it doesn't
exist yet).

path.description:
A path prefix being typed, relative to `base` (e.g. `An`). Suggestions are
directories inside the vault only.

base.description:
A vault-relative directory the suggestions are rooted at and returned
relative to — e.g. the taxonomy root for a type's folder path, which is
stored relative to it. Defaults to the vault root.

language.description:
The user's language preference (may carry a script subtag, e.g.
`zh-Hant`) — picks the language of the preset display text (labels,
descriptions, category headers). English when absent or untranslated.

categories.description: Categories in display order — the picker renders a group per entry.

TypePresetSummary.description:
One built-in type the picker can offer. Metadata only: the concrete
[`EntityTypeConfig`] comes from the resolve endpoint, since it depends on the
chosen title language and which other presets are being added alongside it.

id.description:
Stable preset id — also the default [`EntityTypeConfig::id`] and the key a
client uses to match an already-added type (id equality). Never localized.

label.description:
Display label in the requested `language` (English for languages the
presets aren't written in). Localized by the core — presets seed user
data, so their text ships with the registry rather than client catalogs.

description.description:
One-line, plain-language description for the picker card, localized like
`label`.

providers.description: Providers this preset wires up, in priority order — rendered as chips.

relationTargets.description:
Preset ids this type links to via relation fields (e.g. `["franchise"]`).
Drives the picker's "pairs well with" suggestions entirely client-side.

TypePresetCategory.description:
A preset category — the "what do you want to track?" grouping. A flat string
enum (not doc-commented variants) so swift-openapi-generator renders proper
Swift cases, matching `FieldType`/`DateRole`.

TypePresetProvider.description: A provider chip on a preset card (id + display label from the catalog).

TypePresetCategoryInfo.description:
A category with its display label (localized like the preset labels), so the
picker can render group headers without hardcoding the set. Order in the
response is the display order.

ResolveTypePresetsRequest.description:
Request to materialize one or more presets into concrete types, merged against
the schema the client currently holds (empty during onboarding). Stateless: the
endpoint reads no vault, so onboarding and the settings editor call it the same
way.

currentTypes.description:
The types already in the editor/vault. Used to wire relations, detect
id/path collisions, and propose back-fills. Empty for a fresh vault.

presetIds.description: Preset ids the user selected, in the order to add them.

language.description:
The language for the new types, as a user-language preference code (may
carry a script subtag, e.g. `zh-Hant`). The **single** language choice —
both derivations flow from it: its bare primary subtag is stamped as the
title/filename/season language, and it picks the language of the seeded
*text* (labels, status values, folder names, shelf titles) for the
languages the presets ship. Other languages still stamp their titles but
fall back to English text (e.g. `ko`: Korean titles, English labels).
Script subtags affect text glyphs only — stored keys stay bare `zh`.
Absent → English throughout.

ResolveTypePresetsResponse.description:
The result of resolving presets: ready-to-insert types plus proposed edits to
existing types. The client shows any back-fills/collisions for confirmation and
merges the accepted result into its editor state — no merge logic is duplicated
per runtime.

types.description:
New entity types to append, with relations to absent types stripped and
relations to co-selected/existing types kept, and any id/path collisions
already suffixed (see `collisions`).

backfills.description:
Proposed relation fields to add to *existing* types so they can link to a
newly added type (the "add one, then another later" case). Proposals only —
the client applies the ones the user accepts.

homeSections.description: Home sections (one per added type) the client can offer to add to Home.

collisions.description:
Presets whose id/path collided with an existing type and were suffixed, so
the UI can surface a rename.

TypePresetBackfill.description: A proposed relation field to add to an existing type.

typeId.description: The existing type to add the field to.

presetId.description: The preset (newly added) that this relation targets.

field.description: The relation field to add to `type_id`.

TypePresetCollision.description: A preset whose default id/path collided with an existing type and was suffixed.

userLanguages.description:
The language-picker options the preference is chosen from; every
language-sensitive behavior (UI locale, title language, provider request
language) derives from the picked entry.

Language.description:
A title-language option for the schema editor: an ISO 639-1 `code`. The
display name is rendered client-side from the code with the platform's
localized language-name API (`Locale.localizedString` / `Intl.DisplayNames`),
so it follows the UI language instead of being a hardcoded English exonym.
See [`crate::languages`].

UserLanguage.description:
A user-language preference option for the clients' single language picker:
the preference code (which, unlike a title language, may carry a script
subtag — `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant`), its endonym label, and the bare title/content
language it maps to. Whether the UI is *translated* into a code is a
per-client build fact, not core data, so each client derives it from its own
shipped-locale set. See [`crate::languages`].

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date, so date-relative
home-section criteria (`today() - "30d"`) are judged against the user's day
rather than the host's clock. Falls back to the host's local date.

criteria.description: The section's criteria, echoed from the config when defined.

tags.description:
The entity's built-in tags (the frontmatter `tags` list). Always present
(empty when none) so clients can render it without a null check.

episodeProgress.description:
Watched/total for the type's episodes section, when it declares one — a
resident derived stat (computed at parse time) so list/grid views can show
progress without reading bodies. `None` for types without episodes.

status.description:
The entity's resolved lifecycle status — present only when the type declares
an `enumRole: status` field and the entity carries a value for it. Resolved
at parse time (see [`crate::status::resolve_status`]) so feed/filters/badges
read it without re-deriving. `None` for types without a status field.

EpisodeProgress.description: A watched/total count for an entity's episodes/tracks section.

ResolvedStatus.description:
An entity's resolved status: the status field's name, the raw user value, and
the canonical it maps to (`None` when the value is unmapped or no mapping is
configured). Present on [`EntitySummary`] only when the type declares a status
field and the entity carries a value for it.

CanonicalStatus.description:
The small fixed set of lifecycle statuses the engine can reason about. User
option strings map onto these via [`StatusValues`]; an entity's own value may
resolve to `None` (unmapped) and is still preserved. `Paused` and `Dropped` sit
*outside* the planning→ongoing→completed progression (see
[`CanonicalStatus::rank`]); both are suppressed from "up next" (a paused/dropped
thing isn't something to act on now), but `Paused` still auto-resumes on a log
while `Dropped` never does.

CanonicalStatusCounts.description:
Entity counts per canonical lifecycle status (schema-driven per type via
`statusValues`), scoped like the rest of the stats response. Entities with
no status field, no value, or an unmapped value are counted in none of them.
Fixed fields (not a map) for codegen-friendliness, mirroring [`StatusValues`].

AnalyticsActivity.description:
Year-over-year activity: a year × month matrix of dated entities, filterable
by type. Backs the statistics heatmap + per-year totals. (Browsing dated
entities by period lives in the calendar's year/season views; this is the
at-a-glance cross-year comparison.)

totalDated.description: Distinct entities with at least one parseable date.

types.description: Type filter options (types that have dated entities), most first.

years.description: Per-year rows, most recent year first.

total.description: Dated occurrences in the year across all types.

months.description:
Twelve monthly counts (Jan..Dec) across all types. Year-only dates count
toward `total` but not toward any month bucket.

byType.description: Per-type monthly breakdown, for the type filter.

months.description: Twelve monthly counts (Jan..Dec) for this type within the year.

today.description:
The client's **local** date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), so the date-relative
status-mismatch queue ("completed in the future", "missed event") is scoped
to the user's today rather than UTC. Defaults to the server's UTC date.

brokenAssets.description: Entities whose local cover path points to a file that no longer exists.

statusMismatch.description:
Entities whose canonical status contradicts a dated field: a `completed`
entity with a completion/event date in the *future* (impossible), or a still
-`planning` entity whose *event* date has already passed (a missed event you
probably forgot to update). Date-relative, so computed against the client's
local `today`.

duplicateFilenames.description:
Entities whose filename collides with another entity's after wikilink
normalization (NFC, case-insensitive, last path segment). Such names are
ambiguous targets for `[[wikilinks]]` — a bare `[[Name]]` resolves to only
one of them — so they're surfaced for renaming. Grouped so colliding
entries sit adjacent.

id.description:
Stable machine id (e.g. `missing-cover`); the client localizes the display
label from this. The core intentionally emits no English queue text.

CalendarDay.description:
One day in the month grid. Its `items` are already collapsed per entity — the
same `(date, entity)` merge the activity feed uses ([`ActivityItem`]) — so a
single entity that has a dated field, an aired episode, and a daily-note
mention on this day is one item with three entries, not three items.

ActivityItem.description:
One reverse-chronological activity item: everything that happened to a single
entity on a single date, collapsed together. A daily-note mention, a
started/completed date stamp, and episode air/completion dates that share a
`(date, entity)` all land in one item's `entries`.

ActivityEntry.description:
A constituent of an [`ActivityItem`], discriminated by `source` — the same
flat-struct-plus-discriminator shape as [`CalendarEntry`] (the contract has no
tagged enums). Only the fields for that source are populated.

dateField.description: `taxonomy`: the date field's name, its raw value, and its resolved role.

notePath.description: `daily-note`: the note path and the mention snippets for this entity/date.

episodeRole.description:
`episode`: the air-vs-completion role, the schema section heading, and the
episodes sharing this date (a binge collapses into one entry).

CalendarEntrySource.description:
Identifies whether a calendar entry came from taxonomy metadata, a daily
note, or a dated episode/track in the entity body.

EpisodeDateRole.description:
Which episode date a calendar placement came from: the air/release date
(`📅`, "scheduled") or the completion date (`✅`, "completed").

cursor.description: Opaque `YYYY-MM` cursor from the previous page.

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date — so `recent` /
`up-next` / `catch-up` are judged against the user's day rather than a UTC
server clock. Falls back to the server's UTC date.

limit.description:
Target number of items per page (1–100, default 20). A page gathers whole
months until it holds at least this many, so a sparse feed (one item each in
scattered months) fills a single page instead of one request per month.

mode.description:
`all` (default), `recent`, `up-next`, or `catch-up` (past planning dates
still in `planning` status — released/aired, still on your list).

cursor.description:
The next cursor (`YYYY-MM`) to load the following page, or `None` at the
end of the feed.

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date — so "upcoming" is
judged against the user's day rather than a UTC server clock (matters for a
reminder that fires at a local morning). Falls back to the server's UTC date.

months.description:
Horizon: how many non-empty months of upcoming items to include (1–12,
default 3). Items are ascending, so the soonest come first.

UpcomingResponse.description:
The upcoming-window feed: future release/planning dates and scheduled episode
air dates within a horizon, ascending and flattened (no cursor). Daily-note
mentions are excluded — this is the "what's coming" source for the Home "Coming
up" section and the iOS reminder scheduler. Reuses [`ActivityItem`], so each
item already carries the entity (its `title` + `titles` map for localization +
cover `image`) and the date's source (a date field with its role, or the
episodes airing that day).

credentials.description:
Credential fields this provider needs. Empty for keyless providers. The
frontend and iOS render their credential editors from this list rather
than hard-coding per-provider inputs — core is the single source.

searchSupported.description:
Whether the provider supports free-text search. `false` means it only
resolves a pasted URL/ID (the query box should hint that to the user).

ExternalProviderCredentialField.description:
One credential input a provider requires (e.g. an API key). The `key` is the
secret-store key (also the `KIZUNASHELF_<UPPER_KEY>` env var on web/desktop).

secret.description: Render as a masked/password input and never echo back the stored value.

required.description: A required credential gates the provider; an optional one only refines it.

language.description:
The viewer's language preference (may carry a script subtag —
`zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant`). Providers that localize honor it.

searchSupported.description: Whether the provider supports free-text search (vs. URL/ID resolution only).

reason.description:
Why the provider is disabled (no mapping, missing credentials, …). Absent
when the provider is enabled.

error.description:
Set when this provider was queried but its request failed, so the UI can
surface "search failed" instead of silently implying zero results. One
failing provider never fails the whole search.

ExternalMatch.description:
A search result: the raw candidate plus its schema-resolved field and body
previews for a specific entity type.

entityType.description:
The entity type this candidate was resolved against. Always set — with a
concrete `type` it echoes that type; in cross-type (`all`) search it is the
type whose schema produced these field/body previews.

existing.description: The existing library entity this candidate already maps to, if any.

MappedFieldValue.description:
One field's value resolved from a candidate against the entity-type schema.
The core does the schema-driven mapping (field-type normalization, list vs
scalar, `externalRef`→url, date→season) so every runtime applies identical
values; clients add only the human-facing label.

value.description: The resolved value: a scalar for scalar fields, an array for list fields.

source.description: The external source (provider id) the value came from.

externalField.description:
The provider field the value was read from. Absent for an `externalRef`
field (its value is the candidate URL, not a metadata field).

hasValue.description: Whether the resolved value carries content (drives default selection).

MappedBodySection.description:
A body-section heading filled from a candidate's metadata, pre-rendered to
Markdown. Clients merge it into the entity body (replace/append by heading).

ExistingEntityRef.description:
A library entity a candidate already resolves to, via one of the entity's
`externalRef` fields matching the candidate's provider + URL/id. Lets the UI
mark a result "in library" and link straight to it instead of re-adding.

QuickAddRequest.description:
Quick-add: create a library entity directly from an external search candidate
in one server-side step — schema-map its fields/body, derive a safe filename,
download covers (fail-safe), and import episodes (fail-safe). The client echoes
the candidate it picked from search; the core re-runs the schema mapping itself
and never trusts client-mapped values.

basename.description:
Override the derived basename. When absent, the core derives it from the
type's filename title language (falling back to the candidate title).

language.description:
The viewer's language preference (may carry a script subtag), used for the
fail-safe episode import so episode titles arrive localized.

alreadyExisted.description:
True when the candidate already resolved to a library entity (via an
external ref) and nothing new was created — the returned entity is the
existing one, so the client just navigates to it.

basenameAdjusted.description: True when a title collision forced a disambiguated basename (` (2023)`, …).

cover.description:
Per-cover download outcomes. A failed cover keeps its remote URL in
frontmatter (fail-safe) and never fails the request.

tags.description:
The entity's built-in tags (the frontmatter `tags` list). Always present
(empty when none) so clients can render it without a null check.

episodeProgress.description:
Watched/total for the type's episodes section, when it declares one — a
resident derived stat (computed at parse time) so list/grid views can show
progress without reading bodies. `None` for types without episodes.

status.description:
The entity's resolved lifecycle status — present only when the type declares
an `enumRole: status` field and the entity carries a value for it. Resolved
at parse time (see [`crate::status::resolve_status`]) so feed/filters/badges
read it without re-deriving. `None` for types without a status field.

sourceUrl.description: Source URL that was downloaded (or attempted).

path.description: Vault-relative local path written on success.

message.description: Why the item was skipped or failed.

conflictResolved.description:
True when an existing file referenced by another entity forced a
disambiguated filename.

QuickAddEpisodeResult.description:
The episode-import outcome of a quick-add. Present only when the type declares
an episodes section and the candidate's provider supports episodes.

error.description:
A fetch/import failure. The entity is still created; the client can retry
from the detail page.

canonicalStatus.description:
Filter to one canonical lifecycle status (`planning`/`ongoing`/…),
resolved per type from its `statusValues` — usable with or without `type`
for cross-type status shelves.

updatedLinks.description:
Present only for a rename that repointed `[[wikilinks]]` in other managed
files (configured type folders, daily notes, and list pages): how many
links changed and across how many files. Absent for non-rename updates and
for renames that touched nothing, so a client can show "Updated N links"
only when it happened.

RenameLinkUpdate.description:
Tally of the wikilink repointing a rename performed. See
[`EntityMutationResponse::updated_links`].

episodes.description:
The parsed episodes/tracks list, when the entity's type declares an
`episodes` body section. `None` otherwise.

notesBody.description:
The entity body to render in the generic "Notes" view: identical to
`entity.body` except sections that have a dedicated UI (the episodes
section) are removed, so they aren't shown twice. `entity.body` stays the
raw source of truth for editing.

EntityEpisodes.description:
The parsed contents of an entity's episodes/tracks body section: groups
(season/disc sub-headings; ungrouped items land in one unlabeled group) and a
watched/total roll-up. Derived from the Markdown body, which stays the source
of truth.

description.description:
Free-text Markdown the user wrote *above* the list (between the heading and
the first item/sub-heading); empty when there is none. Shown by the
dedicated episodes UI since the body's generic render drops this section.

trailing.description: Free-text Markdown *below* the last list item; empty when there is none.

label.description: Sub-heading label (season/disc); empty for the ungrouped group.

key.description:
The episode/track number or identifier (e.g. `0`, `12.5`, `OVA1`); may be
empty for an item with no parseable number.

date.description:
The air/release date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), rendered as an Obsidian Tasks
`📅 YYYY-MM-DD` suffix on the list item. Absent when the provider has no
per-item date (e.g. album tracks).

done.description:
The completion date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), rendered as an Obsidian Tasks
`✅ YYYY-MM-DD` suffix. Stamped when the item is checked and cleared when
unchecked; preserved across external syncs.

ToggleEpisodeRequest.description:
Checks or unchecks a single episode/track, identified by its group label and
key — so toggling watched state sends just the changed item, not the whole
list. Checking stamps `date` as the completion date (`✅`); unchecking clears it.
Independent of daily-note logging (`/log`), which never touches episodes.

group.description: The season/disc group label of the episode (empty for the ungrouped list).

key.description:
The episode/track key within the group (its number/identifier). Used to
locate the item when it uniquely identifies one; otherwise `index` wins.

index.description:
The item's 0-based position within its group — the fallback locator when
`key` is empty or duplicated (titles can repeat too, so position is the
stable tiebreaker; the revision guard keeps it valid).

date.description:
The completion date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to stamp when checking — **required**, the
client's local date, so the `✅` matches the user's day rather than a UTC
server clock. Ignored when unchecking. Re-checking a watched episode with a
different `date` is how the completion date is edited.

provider.description: Provider id to fetch from; defaults to the entity's first episode source.

language.description:
Preferred episode-title language: the viewer's language preference, which
may carry a script subtag (`zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant`). Providers that support
translations honor it, normalizing to whatever their API distinguishes.

EpisodeSyncResponse.description:
Response of the episodes `fetch`: the providers that can supply episodes for
this entity, plus the structured episodes from the chosen one.

provider.description: The provider these `groups` came from (empty when there are no sources).

EpisodeSource.description:
A provider that can supply episodes for an entity (it supports episode import
and the entity has a matching external ref with a value).

label.description: Season/disc label (e.g. "Season 1"); empty for a flat provider.

date.description:
The item's air/release date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) when the provider exposes one;
absent otherwise (e.g. CD tracks).

ImportEpisodesRequest.description:
Imports provider episodes (the chosen subset, already grouped/flattened by the
client) by merging them into the entity's existing episodes.

overwrite.description:
When true, a matched existing item's title is overwritten with the incoming
one (the client ticked it). Defaults false — matched titles are only filled
when empty, never replacing a hand edit — so older clients keep that behavior.

dryRun.description:
Preview the write without touching disk. `Option` is already optional to
serde; no `#[serde(default)]` (it makes schemars emit a `null` default that
the zod generator can't apply to a boolean).

LogActivityRequest.description:
Logs an activity to the day's daily note, and — for a `started`/`completed`
log — stamps the matching frontmatter date field. Episode watching is a
separate concern (`/episodes/watch`); logging never reads or writes the
episode list.

op.description: `add` (default) records the activity; `remove` is its exact inverse.

revision.description:
The entity's current revision — required whenever the log mutates the
entity: a `started`/`completed` log that stamps a `dateRole` field or flips
a mapped `enumRole: status` field. Ignored for a daily-note-only log.

date.description:
The log's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), **required** — the client supplies the user's
local date, so the server never assumes "today" in UTC and past actions can
be logged.

kind.description:
Whether this records progress, a start, or a completion. Drives the
frontmatter date-stamp; does not affect the daily-note line.

notePath.description: The daily note the line was (or would be) written to.

noteWillBeCreated.description: The note doesn't exist yet and would be created (from the template).

section.description: The heading the line is written under.

lineAlreadyPresent.description: `add`: the exact line is already in the section, so nothing was written.

lineMatched.description: `remove`: whether the exact line was found (and removed). `None` on `add`.

willStampDate.description: The date field this log stamped (`add`) or cleared (`remove`) on the entity.

willFlipStatus.description:
The status this log flips the entity to. Present only for an `add` of a
`started`/`completed` log when the type has a mapped `enumRole: status`
field and the flip is a promotion (never a demotion, never from `dropped`).
Always `None` on `remove` — a status flip has no safe inverse, so removing a
log deliberately leaves status untouched (see `docs/status-role-plan.md`).

entity.description:
The refreshed entity detail when the log mutated the entity (a date stamp or
a status flip). `None` on a daily-note-only log or a dry run.

FlippedStatus.description:
The status field, the value written, and the canonical it represents, for a
log that flips the entity's status.

fields.description:
Restrict to these field names; when omitted, all image fields with remote
URLs are downloaded.

entityType.description: Restrict the batch to one entity type; when omitted, the whole library.

ImportSourceCatalogItem.description: One selectable import source in the catalog.

inputLabel.description: Human label for the input field ("Bangumi username", "Yamtrack CSV export").

providers.description: Provider ids this source resolves items to.

ImportInputKind.description: How an import source receives its input.

ImportJob.description:
An in-memory batch import job. Like the asset-download job it does not survive
a restart; re-running is safe because the dedup gate skips already-created
entities. `plan` is populated once `status` reaches `planned`.

ImportPlanBucket.description:
A source "bucket" (the provider's own media kind, e.g. Bangumi `anime`) and
the entity types it can map to. One candidate type is auto-selected; several
leave `selected_type` empty for the user to pick.

ImportPlanItemState.description: A planned item's disposition against the resident library.

ImportReviewReason.description: Why a planned item needs manual review.

ImportPlanUserData.description: The user data resolved for a planned item, summarized for the review UI.

ImportInput.description:
Input for a source fetch: a username (profile sources) or the pasted text of
a CSV export (CSV sources). CSV arrives as a string field, not multipart, so
the generated clients and the iOS in-process tunnel stay trivial.

language.description:
The viewer's language preference (request context, not user-entered),
used to localize review-list display titles where the source distinguishes
languages (e.g. Bangumi's `name`/`name_cn`). Mirrors the external-search
`language` param. Optional; absent falls back to the source default.

types.description: Bucket → chosen entity type id, for buckets with multiple candidate types.

ImportDecision.description:
A per-item override applied at commit: force a create/skip, choose a target
type (for ambiguous buckets), or supply a hand-picked candidate for a
`needsReview` item.

entityType.description: Restrict the plan to one entity type; when omitted, the whole library.

AssetDownloadPlanItem.description:
One remote image awaiting download, returned by the `plan` endpoint so a host
(e.g. iOS) can fetch it itself — via a background `URLSession` — instead of
having the core download it through `reqwest`.

listKey.description:
For image-list fields, the element's URL (used to derive a stable
filename); absent for single image fields.

revision.description: Entity revision at plan time (advisory; ingest re-reads the entity).

AssetIngestRequest.description:
Hands the core one externally-downloaded image to validate, place under the
vault, and write into a single frontmatter field.

listKey.description: Present iff `field` is an image-list field; the list element's URL.

sourcePath.description:
Absolute host path of the file the client already downloaded. The core
reads it directly (like `indexCacheDir`) and deletes it afterward.

contentType.description: Content-Type the host observed, used as an image sniff hint.

revision.description: Advisory; ingest re-reads the entity rather than enforcing this.

AssetUploadRequest.description:
Places raw image bytes a web/desktop client picked from the device under the
entity's asset directory. Unlike download/ingest, the core only *places* the
file and returns its vault-relative path — it does not rewrite frontmatter.
The editor stages that path into its draft and persists it on the normal save.

listKey.description:
Reserved for callers; the core derives a stable content-hash key for
image-list elements regardless.

contentType.description: Client-observed Content-Type, used as an image-type/extension hint.

filename.description: Original filename, used only as an extension fallback.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the placed asset.

conflictResolved.description:
Whether the destination collided with another entity's asset and was
disambiguated.

TagsResponse.description:
The vault's full tag vocabulary (sorted, deduped) — backs tag autocomplete in
the editor and the Library tag filter.

entity.description:
When set, each summary reports whether it contains this entity id
(membership for the entity page's "manage lists").

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date, so smart-list
`itemCount`/`contains` with `today()` criteria are judged against the
user's day. Falls back to the host's local date.

ListSummary.description:
One row in the lists index. `description` is the prose above the first list;
`itemCount` and `ordered` summarize the list without its full contents.

id.description:
Stable identifier: the list file's basename (without its extension).
Static and smart lists are separate id namespaces (different detail
endpoints), so the same basename may appear once per kind.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the Markdown file.

itemCount.description: Total item count across every section.

sectionCount.description: Number of named (`## heading`) sections; `0` for a flat list.

contains.description:
Whether the list contains the entity named by the `entity` query param.
Only present when that param was supplied (drives the entity page's
"manage lists" membership toggles); omitted otherwise.

ListKind.description:
Which kind of list a summary row is: a hand-curated Markdown list or a
criteria-driven smart list (`.base` file). The two live in the same index
but are served by different detail endpoints.

ListDetail.description:
A list's full editable state: description, its sections (each with its own
heading, marker style, and resolved items), and the trailing Markdown.
`revision` guards writes.

ListSection.description:
One section of a list: an optional `## heading`, its marker style, and the
resolved items beneath it. `heading` is `null` for the ungrouped block of items
above the first heading (and for a flat list, which is a single such section).

ListMarker.description:
How a list section renders: plain bullets, a numbered list, or a task list
with checkboxes. Per-section, since each Markdown list block is independent.

ListItem.description:
One item of a list. `text` is the Markdown content after the list marker (and
after any task checkbox), preserving annotations; `target` is the first
wikilink target in it; `entity` is the resolved entity when the target matches
an indexed note (else `null`); and `checked` is the task state for items in a
`todo` section (`null` for non-task items).

UpdateListRequest.description:
Full rewrite of a list (reorder within and across sections, section add/rename,
per-section marker toggle, description/trailing edits, item removal). The server
renders the whole body from these parts, so the section and item order is
authoritative.

ListSectionInput.description:
One section as supplied by the client on a full list rewrite: an optional
heading (`null`/empty for the ungrouped block), its marker style, and its items
in their authoritative order.

ListItemInput.description:
One item as supplied by the client on a full list rewrite. Only the raw `text`
is sent; the server re-derives the target/entity on the next read.

checked.description: Task state for an item in a `todo` section; `null`/omitted otherwise.

AddListItemRequest.description:
Adds a single entity to a list's first list block. Used cross-page (from an
entity detail page), so it carries no client revision — it reads the file
fresh, appends, and writes. The server computes the disambiguated wikilink.

scope.description:
Entity type id to scope the new list to (writes the `file.inFolder`
atom and derives the grid view's cover image from the type's schema).

SmartListDetail.description:
A smart list's full editable state. `warnings` lists every construct in
the underlying `.base` file that the app ignores (unsupported filters,
views, sorts) — all of it preserved on save.

scope.description:
The entity type this list is scoped to, when the file carries the
recognized `file.inFolder(<type folder>)` idiom; `null` = all types.

SmartListView.description:
One view of a smart list — a named tab with its own layout, extra filters
(AND-ed with the global criteria), sort, and result limit.

image.description: Cards image property reference (grid views), e.g. `note.cover`.

SmartViewLayout.description:
The app layout of one smart-list view: `list` ⇔ a Bases `table` view,
`grid` ⇔ a Bases `cards` view.

SmartSortSpec.description:
One sort key of a smart-list view. `property` is a Bases property
reference: `note.<field>`, `file.name`, or `file.mtime`.

SmartListPreviewRequest.description:
Evaluates an unsaved smart-list definition — the live preview while the
rule builder is open. Returns the standard entity page shape.

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date, so `today()`
date criteria are judged against the user's day rather than the host's
clock. Falls back to the host's local date.

UpdateSmartListRequest.description:
Full rewrite of a smart list's criteria and views. Constructs the editor
doesn't model (`unsupported` rules, non-table/cards views, unknown YAML
keys) are preserved server-side.

view.description: View (tab) name to evaluate; defaults to the file's first supported view.

today.description:
Today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the client's **local** date, so `today()`
date criteria are judged against the user's day rather than the host's
clock. Falls back to the host's local date.
